failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: The passages held a verbatim archive answer ('a eucalyptus tree'; '...ILLNESS, GERMANY.'). The agent trimmed it to 'Eucalyptus' or swapped in a 'more accurate' name, 'German Empire', so Rule 3's copy-exactly instruction lost to Rule 4 trimming and the agent's own knowledge.

rejected_edits.content: - PRECEDENCE: a verbatim archive answer beats every Rule 4 trimming rule and any 'more accurate' name from your own knowledge. Copy it exactly as printed, including a leading article, a type noun, or a plain country name. In flat flashcard dumps (StudyStack and similar) the answer is the capitalized words after the clue's last word, often after a comma. Strip only a contestant tag such as 'right: Name'.
rejected_edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.

rejected_edits.content: - 'They/It were once called "X" (after the town or person Y)' or 'formerly known as X': the subject pronoun is the THING that carried the old name. Answer with that thing's current common name (the food, object, group or title), never the place, person or old name already in the clue. Passages that say '<X>, now known as <name>' give it. The origin place or inventor is an anchor.
rejected_edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').

rejected_edits.content: - A clue that is only a head of state's or ruler's title and name, with biographical passages, asks for the COUNTRY or state he or she leads. Do not answer with the title phrase or the person's own name.
rejected_edits.target: Give the bare name ('Ronald Reagan'), not the event, the place or the date.
